Modify a plotly figure in Shiny without re-rendering it

Source: R/shiny.R
plotlyProxy.Rd

plotlyProxy() refers to a plot rendered with renderPlotly(); plotlyProxyInvoke() calls a plotly.js function on it, e.g. "restyle", "relayout", "update", "addTraces", "deleteTraces", "extendTraces" or "animate". Arguments are passed to the plotly.js function after the plot element (see https://plotly.com/javascript/plotlyjs-function-reference/); "reconfig" sets a new config.

Usage

plotlyProxy(
  outputId,
  session = shiny::getDefaultReactiveDomain(),
  deferUntilFlush = TRUE
)

plotlyProxyInvoke(p, method, ...)

Arguments

outputId

The output id of the plot.

session

The Shiny session.

deferUntilFlush

Send the message after Shiny's next flush (so the plot exists).

p

A proxy from plotlyProxy().

method

A plotly.js function name.

...

Arguments to the plotly.js function. Graph objects and data frames are serialised like figures (data frames as rows).

Value

The proxy, invisibly for plotlyProxyInvoke().

Examples

if (interactive() && requireNamespace("shiny", quietly = TRUE)) {
  ui <- shiny::fluidPage(shiny::actionButton("add", "Add a point"), plotlyOutput("plot"))
  server <- function(input, output, session) {
    output$plot <- renderPlotly(go_figure(go_scatter(y = c(1, 3, 2))))
    shiny::observeEvent(input$add, {
      plotlyProxy("plot", session) |>
        plotlyProxyInvoke("extendTraces", list(y = list(list(stats::runif(1)))), list(0))
    })
  }
  shiny::shinyApp(ui, server)
}
